title: Deployment control plane: fine-grained canary, shadowing, and rollback across environments
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Objective: Build a unified deployment control plane that supports canary rollouts, A/B traffic splits, shadow traffic, and automatic rollback policies with consistent behaviour across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments, while accounting for environment-specific constraints (networking, capacity isolation, and control-plane reachability).

Scope:
- Control plane APIs to declare rollout policies (percentage-based canaries, weighted A/B, shadow sinks, success criteria) and an operator to apply them across environments.
- Traffic splitting layer that can operate in-host (Hosted routing proxy), at the edge for Dedicated, and as a policy shim for Private (where customers may run a local proxy).
- Auto-rollback triggers based on configurable SLO/SLA breaches, error-rate spikes, latency regressions, and custom health checks.
- Observability hooks and per-route metrics (token-level latency, error-classification) to drive rollback decisions.
- Migration plan for parity: when a policy cannot be applied exactly in Private due to network constraints, provide a deterministic fallback and explicit operator warnings.

Non-goals: performing model evaluation for quality (that is handled by Optimize/evals), or implementing new model checkpointing semantics. This ticket focuses on runtime routing and orchestration behavior and the API surface for rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: API spec published for rollout policies (canary, weighted A/B, shadow) and rollback rules and approved by PM and Security
End-to-end canary rollout completes in Hosted and Dedicated: 0->5%->25%->100% with expected traffic shaping and metrics surfaced in Console
Shadow traffic supports non-destructive replication of 10% of requests to a target model in Hosted and Dedicated; Private supports shadowing when customer proxy is configured
Auto-rollback fires and halts rollout on predefined thresholds (5xx rate > 1.5x baseline OR p95 latency regressed > 40%) and logged as an incident with automatic mitigation action
Console shows per-rollout metrics and a clear diff of model versions, traffic weights, and the reason for any rollback
Integration tests for routing behaviors added to CI with simulated Dedicated and Private stubs and results flaking <2% over three runs

implementation_summary: We will add a Rollout CRD-like object in the control plane with a stable API. Adapters will translate that object into environment-specific actions: Hosted uses in-cluster routing proxies, Dedicated attaches weights at the pool load-balancer, Private uses a lightweight agent that applies local proxy rules. Rollback evaluation will run in a centralized decision service with configurable thresholds and a fallback local enforcement for Private. Metrics ingestion will be extended to include per-rollout windows and smoothing to avoid noisy rollbacks.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Private deployments may be unable to accept push updates due to egress/firewall restrictions. Mitigation: implement a pull-based agent and certify an 'agent-0.1' release for Private customers.
Risk: Rapid rollback storms if multiple rollouts trigger simultaneously. Mitigation: add global concurrency limiter and staggered rollback queue with operator override.

Risk: Observability gaps cause false positives for rollback. Mitigation: require two independent signals (errors + latency OR errors + custom health) before auto-rollback; expose confidence scores in Console.
